clauses.definition: Steps run strictly in order. Step k+1 starts delay_before_ms after every attempt of step k has resolved.
Every first-attempt request in a step is built, then one event releases all of them. Send order is unspecified.
attempt_timeout_ms is a planned client-side total timeout. On expiry the connection closes, the attempt outcome is timeout, and the trial is never aborted.
Attempt n+1 is sent backoff_ms[n] after attempt n resolves when that outcome is in retry_on. Body and event id are unchanged; the signature is regenerated.
W = sum over steps of (delay_before_ms + max over the step's deliveries of sum over attempts of (attempt_timeout_ms + backoff_ms)). W <= 25000 ms, below the 30000 ms execution deadline.

If the 30000 ms execution deadline passes before every planned attempt is dispatched and resolved, in-flight attempts are cancelled, nothing further is dispatched, and execution_deadline_exceeded, cancelled_attempts and undispatched are recorded.
HMAC-SHA256 hex over the exact body bytes with the resolved secret. A deliberately invalid signature uses key = sha256('duress-invalid:' + delivery_id) hex digest as the HMAC key over the body.
GET /t/{trial}/v1/payments/{id} returns the fixture as 200 JSON, or 404 for an unknown id. Any other prefix returns 410 and is recorded as a stale_call.
Each matching provider call is delayed by ms.

Matching calls are held until parties have arrived (released_by=parties) or timeout_ms has passed since the first arrival (released_by=timeout). Everything held is released at once; later calls are not held.
Evidence kinds answered, group_overlap, attempt_timed_out, retried, send_after_end; effects exactly_once(order,payment) and payment_unchanged(payment); pass condition status_class.
Settlement follows the phased supervisor: clean, drain_unverified, forced, crashed or unconfirmed.
